Class Schedule Dec 11 - Dec 17 ‹ S 11 M 12 T 13 W 14 T 15 F 16 S 17 › Welcome to YOGA UNION Baltimore YOGA UNION is a community yoga space dedicated to providing the highest-quality group and private yoga classes, workshops, and events. We are a women-owned, independent small business, looking to bring a safe, inclusive yoga space back to Baltimore City. Our owners are trained in lineages that are hard to find in the Baltimore area and our staff is comprised of loving and talented teachers — each bringing with them a unique background and creative style. We have something for everyone! ​ At YOGA UNION we believe that yoga is for every body — all races, body types, sizes, abilities, genders, sexualities, ages, and ethnicities. ​ We believe that yoga should be available to all, regardless of social or economic status — if finances are a barrier to you practicing yoga, please email us at yogaunionbaltimore@gmail.com . ​ ​ All of our classes happen in the studio and also streaming with Zoom. Where to Find Us Address 1750 Union Ave Suite D Baltimore, MD 21211 Contact yogaunionbaltimore@gmail.com 443-938-4823 (Voicemail only, please email for faster response) PARKING is located on the back side of the building. Make a right turn between the two buildings (past the brick brewery) and follow that down toward the rear of the buildings. You can also access this same parking lot by making a right turn past the building and continuing around to the back, but this route is more narrow and may be occupied by construction vehicles. Feel free to park under I-83 facing the Jones Falls or along the back wall of the building. Please do not block the loading docks. Parking is not reserved and on a first come, first served basis. Yoga Union has two (2) reserved parking spots in the front of the building. If there is a circumstance for which you would require one of these spaces, please contact us before your visit. Please DO NOT park in a space that has a reserved sign for another business, even during evenings and weekend hours. ​ We are just a few steps away from the Woodberry Light Rail stop, Bus Route 21 (Clipper Rd at Union Ave), and the Jones Falls Bike Trail, which runs from the Inner Harbor to Mt. Washington. exterior day front door plant window A photo showing places to park exterior night lobby Packages & Memberships We've got packages and membership options to fit every budget—whether you practice once a month, or every day. Compare Plans seated.png I need to relax and breathe... Yin or Restorative These classes are calm and focus on stillness, breathing, and gentle stretching. Also a great choice if you are looking to relieve stress or anxiety or have mobility issues. READ MORE triangle.png It's been a while since I've practiced and I'm recovering from an injury... Slow Flow or Hatha These classes will explore more physically challenging asana while still offering options for everyone in the room. READ MORE wheel.png I'm ready to challenge my body and mind... Flow, Rocket, Pilates These classes can be faster paced and offer opportunities for advanced asana and inversions. READ MORE We pride ourselves on having the most inclusive classes in Baltimore. That being said, even our most gentle public classes require students to be able to get up and down off of the floor multiple times, unassisted. The studio is also located on an unevenly paved road and some of the parking lot is gravel. If you do not meet these requirements, please inquire about a private session. Meet Your Teachers | Yoga Union Baltimore top of page Instagram Facebook Log In Meet Your Teachers yin cadie 1_edited.png Teacher, Founder & Co-Owner Cadie Bridges-Palmer C-IAYT, E- RYT500, YACEP, Rocket Yoga® I was introduced to yoga in the early 90's during my time as a competitive gymnast and did my first teacher training in 2005. I'm trained in Rocket, Ashtanga, Hatha, Hot Power, 26+2, Pilates Mat, Vinyasa, and Yin Yoga as well as Yoga Therapy, Somatic Healing, and Corrective Exercise. My public offerings are a mix of all these styles with the goal of teaching you how to take your yoga practice off the mat. I also offer 1-on-1 sessions, including Thai Yoga (assisted stretching) and Therapeutic Yoga. steph.jpg Teacher, Founder & Co-Owner Stephanie Fabian, E-RYT500, YACEP, Katonah Yoga® I started my yoga journey as a dancer coming off an injury in 2001 very much approaching the mat for just a physical practice. Instead, I have been able to unlock my imagination and allow my mind to connect to my body. My public offerings include a mix of Pilates, Hatha, Vinyasa, Yin, Chair, Restorative, Breathwork, and Katonah Yoga. I completed my 200-hour training with Katie Thorworth, and then completed my 300-hour certification and an additional 200 hours of Katonah Yoga Training in 2021. I'm available for private sessions of asana and pranayama. abby_edited.jpg Yoga Teacher Abby Chow My yoga journey began in 2012. I completed my 200-hour vinyasa-based yoga teacher training through Red Lila School of Yoga under the guidance of Lindsay Kiracofe, Kate Manchester, and Marissa Walch. As a lifelong learner, I believe that teaching is a practice of continual growth, and I am committed to expanding my knowledge through reading, continuing education, and learning alongside teachers and students. My classes are welcoming to practitioners of all levels and emphasize the connection between breath and movement, creating a well-rounded, full-body practice that cultivates strength, mobility, balance and mindfulness. andrea_edited.jpg Yoga Teacher Andrea Gauld I started practicing yoga in 2012 to supplement triathlon training. Five years later, I completed my 200-hour teacher training along side Stephanie and after encouragement by Cadie to sign up! My focus is to encourage an accessible practice for all students with the use of props and variations of poses. Living in a larger body myself, it is my mission to ensure all teachers are able to create a safe and accessible space for larger body students to practice yoga. ang_edited.jpg Yoga Teacher Ang Baker My personal yoga and meditation practice began in 2004 and remains a sacred and ever evolving gift. In 2024, I enrolled in Yoga Union’s 200 hour yoga teacher training to deepen my practice and study of yogic philosophy. I am beyond grateful for the wonderful teachers, fellow students and friends, and the community we continue to build. I am a Certified Sound Therapist (300 hrs) and offer restorative environments to ground and relax the body and nervous system. My goal is to provide a safe and inclusive space where people can build community and feel welcome, autonomous, and accommodated. anjul_edited_edited.jpg Yoga Teacher Anjul Vij My yoga journey began in 2018, when I was first introduced to yoga by my father. While the initial experience with yoga felt slow and unengaging, everything changed during the COVID-19 pandemic. This period became a turning point, helping me recognize yoga as a powerful discipline that nurtures the connection between mind, body and soul. Motivated by this deeper understanding, I pursued my formal teacher training at the prestigious Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga (MDNIY), under the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India. I further refined my practice and teaching under the guidance of Dr. Ramesh Adhikari, a PhD scholar in Yoga Science & Wellness, followed by travel to Rishikesh, India to further practice and understand yoga and meditation in detail. I specialize in Hatha Yoga, Ashtanga Yoga, Pranayama and Meditation with experience of teaching individuals across all age groups. My aim is to help students experience yoga not just as a physical exercise, but as a holistic lifestyle that promotes long-term well-being. IMG_6068.jpeg Meditation Teacher Ella Baker I’m a dharma teacher in the Kwan Um School of Zen. When I’m not silently sitting on my ass, I write poems, explore nature with my wife, and endlessly serve our two spoiled cats. Outside of zen, I am the founding director of a high school and also serve as the chancellor of a college. To help with this propensity I have to be constantly busy I began practicing contemplative prayer in 2005 and formal meditation in 2007. I took five precepts in the Korean zen tradition in 2021 and ten precepts in 2023. My heart is in bridging cultural gaps, interfaith communication, and removing barriers to access. kamaria_edited.jpg Yoga Teacher Kamaria Joyner In 1999, I bought Bryan Kest’s Power Yoga DVD and I taught myself how to practice yoga. In 2016, I earned an RYT-200 certification from Sterling Hot Yoga in Puerto Morelos, Mexico. In 2020, I completed a 500 hr. teacher training and a Prenatal/Postnatal Yoga teacher training certification. During my 22 years as a yoga student, I learned that there are Eight Limbs of yoga and many ways to practice. I am very proud that my resume includes teaching different styles of yoga to diverse populations because yoga is for Every Body. kate_edited.jpg Yoga Teacher Kate Lynch I came to yoga in 2017 as a fitness skeptic looking to reset my relationship with my body after years of managing a serious illness. I quickly discovered that yoga offered much more than physical wellness: it helped me rebuild trust in my body while opening the door to the deeper benefits of connecting breath, focus, and movement. Cadie and Stephanie have been my teachers since 2019, and I received my 200-hour teaching certification from Yoga Union in 2026. I teach inclusive Hatha and Vinyasa classes that respond to the students in the room. My responsibility is to create a space where everyone, regardless of experience or ability, feels a sense of belonging. My classes are calming, playful, reflective, and educational, with plenty of room to make the practice your own. You are welcome, exactly as you are. liz_edited.jpg Yoga & Pilates Teacher Liz Ragland I strive for a joyful and modern take on yogic philosophy, infusing the vinyasa tradition with elements and metaphors from Katonah Yoga ® . My class is dynamic, playful, and imaginative while still accessible to all levels of practitioner. I am committed to holding respectful and sensitive space for all bodies. I am a 500-hour certified (Kim Manfredi/Charm City Yoga) and earned my Katonah Yoga ® certification in 2025 under Nevine Michaan, Dages Juvelier Keates, Kyle Henry, Reni Bickel, and other world-renowned masters; my Mat Pilates certification is through Peak Pilates. maria_edited.jpg Yoga Teacher Maria Simon On a whim, I signed up for my yoga teacher training in the summer of 2013, and the rest is history. I finally found my voice and direction at a time that I had felt lost. I look at a yoga class as a dancing meditation and incorporate playlists in each practice. After completing my 200-hour yoga teacher training, I immediately continued on to finish my 500-hour teacher training and am currently studying Ayurveda. meghan_edited_edited.jpg Yoga Teacher Meghan Shippe My journey with Yoga began in 2021, during a time when I was seeking something to ground, strengthen, and empower me. Like many, I was initially drawn to the physical practice, but quickly realized I wanted to explore Yoga more deeply. This led me to complete a 200-hour Hatha Yoga Teacher Training at Yoga Union Baltimore. I currently teach accessible and inclusive flow classes. Through teaching, I aim to share the joy, balance, and courage that Yoga continues to bring into my life. myriam_edited.jpg Yoga Teacher Myriam Ralston I have been practicing yoga since 2010 and teaching since 2015 when I finished my initial teacher training in Baptiste-style Vinyasa yoga at the Anthony Bowen YMCA in Washington, DC. In 2020, I completed my 85-hour Prenatal Yoga Teacher Training with YogaWorks in Baltimore, and have been teaching prenatal and post-natal classes virtually and in person ever since. My goal in teaching is to help people with all bodies, backgrounds, and stages of life find the joy, accessibility, and transformative nature of yoga asana and the intentional linking of breath and movement. naomi_edited_edited.jpg Yoga Teacher Naomi Hurley I am a trauma-informed yoga instructor and harm reduction specialist living in Baltimore city. I have a background teaching yoga, meditation, and facilitating therapeutic mindfulness-based support groups at various inpatient addiction treatment centers. niamh_edited_edited.jpg Pilates Teacher Niamh McCormally I was introduced to Yoga in 2001 and was immediately attracted to the therapeutic benefits of the 26&2 series and the heat. In 2014 I earned my RYT 200 designation through Sterling Hot Yoga in Puerto Morales, Mexico, and a few months later I studied for additional certification hours in Yin Yoga through Akasha Yoga and Inferno Hot Pilates. I passionately believe in the benefits: physical and mental, of a yoga practice and I believe that everyone can be transformed by the power of Yoga. raina_edited.jpg Yoga Teacher Raina Runk Bio coming soon... IMG_9574.jpeg Yoga Teacher Sam Jacobson I began my personal yoga practice in 2019 to alleviate pain and stiffness from work and personal life. During the pandemic, my journey evolved into a more introspective practice; connecting mind, body, and breath. I continued learning yoga through group practice which ultimately led me to complete my 200hr-YTT at Yoga Union in 2025. I believe that through intentional movement, breath, and concentration, our practice helps us show up as our best selves off the mat. In class, I encourage each yogi’s agency within their practice while providing gentle guidance and refinement along the way. sherri_edited_edited.jpg Yoga Teacher Sherri Liebrich Kasky I first discovered Yoga 15 years ago, and my practice has helped me grow stronger, more flexible and fearless, both on and off the mat. I strive to combine creative sequencing, which is inspired by my dance training, with a spirit of playfulness and a dose of inspiration to help students deepen their practice. I want to help others thrive in life by nurturing body, mind, and soul with yoga, and hope that you step off the mat feeling refreshed, nourished, and balanced. I completed my 200-hour Vinyasa training in 2018, will always be a student of the practice and am deeply grateful for the loving wisdom my own teachers have shared with me. val_edited_edited.jpg Yoga & Pilates Teacher Valerie Kuehne I was first exposed to yoga while working as a musician and performance artist in NYC in 2009. Over the next 10 years, my practice was mostly inconsistent and purely fitness-based. However, the seed was planted. Since then, I have devoted myself to this practice, which I wholeheartedly believe saved my life. My interest in yoga has bloomed above and beyond acrobatics on the mat, and my goal in teaching is to share aspects of yoga that include philosophy, yogic theory, meditation, pranayama, and shifting one’s perspective to a space of involution, wherein the secrets of the Self emerge. Of course, you can expect quite a few fun inversions, arm balances, backbends, strengthening exercises and twists rolled into a wonderfully creative exploration of our physical bodies and boundaries as well. I hold a 200-hr certification from Yoga Union in Baltimore, and am currently enrolled in a Sound Healing mentorship through Satya Yoga in Columbia. Teacher Training | Yoga Union Baltimore top of page Instagram Facebook Log In Advanced Principles of Practicing and Teaching Yoga 300-hour Training​ Cohort begins in Sept. 2026 (prerequisite is previous completion of a 200-hour program) Yoga Union's 300-hr teacher training has launched. Take your knowledge and teaching to the next level. ​ Cadie and Stephanie will be leading the way through this training. The anatomy portion will be taught by Chris Jamison and we will have a bunch of specialty lecturers. ​ In addition to more in-depth study of Anatomy, Asana, Ethics, and Philosophy we will also be diving in to Yin Yoga, Trauma-Informed practices, History, Sanskrit, Specialty Styles, Planning Workshops, AND MORE. ​ The training is a Fri-Sat-Sun format, one weekend + one day per month for 11 months. ​ ​ ​ All study halls are required. ​ Next Session: ​ 2026 Sept 18-20 Oct 16-18 Nov 6-8 Dec 4-6 Study Hall, 1-3p Dec 20 2027 Jan 8-10 Study Hall, 1-3p Jan 24 Feb 5-7 Study Hall, 1-3p Feb 28 Mar 12-14 Study Hall, 1-3p Mar 28 Apr 9-11 Study Hall, 1-3p Apr 25 May 14-16 Study Hall, 1-3p May 23 Jun 11-13 Study Hall, 1-3p Jun 27 Jul 16-18 Wrap-up and GRADUATION, 1-3p Jul 25 ​ Aug 13-15 and Sept 17-19 Timeslots will be available for anyone who wants to host their final project at the studio. ​ ​ Times: Fridays 6-9p Saturdays 1230-930p Sundays 1-9p ​ ​ Join Us! RYS300_edited.png Foundations of Practicing and Teaching Yoga 200-hour Training​ SOLD OUT Next cohort begins in Sept. 2027 The next installment of Yoga Union's 200-hr teacher training programs will begin in September 2027 under the guidance of Cadie Bridges-Palmer and Stephanie Fabian. ​ The anatomy portion will be taught by Chris Jamison and we will have several guest lecturers. ​ The training is a Fri-Sat-Sun format, one weekend per month for 8 months. ​ ​ Enrollment is limited to ensure everyone can get personal guidance. ​ RYS200-2026seal_edited.png Yin Yoga Immersion 20-hour educational session for teachers and dedicated practitioners. Join us for the Fall Session to learn all about Yin Yoga. This powerful style of yoga is great for athletes, weekend warriors, and anyone in need of a deep stretch and mental reset. ​ Learn the history, anatomy, and applications of Yin Yoga in a small group setting with lots of personal attention. Training will take place over two consecutive weekends. You don't have to be a yoga teacher, but if you are this training counts for 20 CEUs with Yoga Alliance. ​ Next training: October 2, 3, 4 and 9, 10, 11 Times: Friday 6-8p Saturday 1230-4p Sunday 1245-345p Join the Fall Session YACEP (1)_edited.png Yoga Union Baltimore is a Registered Yoga School (RYS) with Yoga Alliance, which designates this teacher training program as one which follows Yoga Alliance’s standards. Students who complete a verified 200- or 300-hr training with this school may be eligible to register with Yoga Alliance as Registered Yoga Teachers (RYT). ​ ​ ​ HOME Plans & Pricing Meet Your Teachers Teacher Training Thai & Private Yoga Types of Yoga FAQ & Etiquette Terms & Policies Join our Mobile App Buy a Gift Card More Use tab to navigate through the menu items. Thai & Private Yoga | Yoga Union Baltimore top of page Instagram Facebook Log In Private Yoga We are available to help you one-on-one with your practice, host your group for a special event, and even come to your workplace to lead a class. office yoga Private and Small Group Sessions Cadie and Stephanie are available to design your perfect practice. From beginners to advanced, just let us know what you need. 1-on-1 sessions can address anything from injury recovery to advanced asana. Group sessions can be tailored to your group, from bridal and birthday celebrations to team-building activities. ​ ​ 30-min 1-on-1 session, $60 60-min 1-on-1 session, $120 60-min Private Group (up to 24 people) class, $150 EMAIL TO BOOK Thai Yoga You may have heard of Stretch Therapy, FST, Assisted Stretch, or Thai Massage... Thai Yoga is a combination of hands-on modalities to promote physical and energetic well-being. Expect a combination of rhythmic compression, gentle yoga postures, and deep stretching to help release tension, improve flexibility, and restore balance. Sessions take place fully clothed on a floor futon. ​ 60-min session with Cadie, $125 Packages available. BOOK ONLINE thai yoga stretch hands assisting Yoga Therapy Yoga therapy is the process of empowering individuals to progress toward improved health and well-being through the application of the teachings and practices of Yoga. It can address parts of the physical, energetic, emotional, and spiritual body that are harder to access in an Asana-based public class. Are you curious about how the other limbs of Yoga can help you function better in day to day life? Email and we can chat. ​ Yoga Therapy is not a replacement for talk therapy or other mental health interventions. Cadie has completed over 1000 hours in the study of Yoga Therapy and is registered with the International Association of Yoga Therapists. She is available to help in all areas within her scope of practice, but her clinical hours focused on Breast Cancer and Transgender care.
